newsitem.title: ITALY: BankItaly study wants wide deficit measure in PSBR.
newsitem.headline: BankItaly study wants wide deficit measure in PSBR.

text.p: A report published by the Bank of Italy on Wednesday urged Italy to broaden its public sector borrowing requirement calculations to include the public administration deficit.

"In forecasting and calculating budgetary policy it would be opportune to shift the emphasis of the borrowing requirement of the state sector to similar indicators related to the public sector...and in particular the public administration," it said.
The report was written by a Bank economist and a member of the European Commission's economic affairs department.
Italy's calculations are based on public sector accounts and not on the public administration accounts that are required by the Maastricht Treaty on Economic and Monetary Union.

Under the treaty, European Union states must cut the ratio between their annual budget deficit and gross domestic product (GDP) to no more than three percent in 1997 to qualify for the planned 1999 launch of a single European currency.

The study said calculations which also took note of public administration accounts provided "a more precise analysis of the PSBR for cost centres, and supplies useful indications for calculations and corrective measures".

The public administration calculation would add some 20 trillion lire, or 0.9 percent of GDP, to the deficit by including tax rebates owed by the government to companies along with back payments due to certain categories of pensioners.

Italy's revised three-year economic programme, which was updated after presentation of the government's 1997 budget designed to cut 62.5 trillion lire off next year's debt, forecasts a 1997 PSBR/GDP ratio of 3.1 percent.
Treasury Undersecretary Laura Pennacchi said earlier this month that Italy's deficit-to-GDP ratio was expected to achieve the three percent goal using the definition applied in the Maastricht treaty.
